global.Ctrl+S: save — straight back to the open file; on a session that has never been saved it opens the save picker
global.u: undo (works everywhere except modals and text entry; while recording, scraps the newest layer — the in-flight pass first, then committed takes one per press — and the transport keeps rolling)
global.Ctrl+R: redo (a peeled take included; recording new material clears redo)
global.recording_automation: mod wheel, pitch bend and channel aftertouch are recorded with the notes, survive every edit and the session file, and play back; X in the piano roll erases them from a clip
global.sustain_pedal: CC64 held during recording becomes note length at commit: releases under the pedal slide to the pedal-up

space_menu.s: save project (save as, always) — opens the save picker: the folder listed, a name line to type into
space_menu.o: open project — opens the file picker on that same folder

preset_browser.description: Space+W on an instrument track. Lists that instrument's saved presets, with a row at the top to save the current panel. Banks live in ~/.phosphor/presets/<instrument>.json, one file per instrument.
preset_browser.Enter_on_save_row: name and save the current panel
preset_browser.Enter_on_preset: load the preset into the track
preset_browser.overwrite: saving under a name the bank already holds rewrites that slot, after a y/n confirmation — names are slots, so no two presets can share one
preset_browser.limits: 128 presets per instrument, 32 characters per name
preset_browser.refusals: a preset is refused rather than loaded when it was saved for a different instrument, with a different number of controls, or against an older panel layout

file_picker.description: the little file tree, opened by space+o (open a project), space+s and first-time ctrl+s (save a project), and a on a sampler pad (load a sound). One folder at a time, listed: no recursive search, no preview, and selecting a row plays nothing. Projects open AND save in one folder — <app dir>/sessions, which is ~/.phosphor/sessions on macOS and Linux and %APPDATA%\phosphor\sessions on Windows, whatever directory you started phosphor from; sounds open on <app dir>/samples.
file_picker.listing: folders first, then files, each half alphabetical and case-insensitive · dot-prefixed names are skipped · files are filtered by what the picker is for (.phos for projects, .wav for sounds, either case) and folders are ALWAYS shown, so you can walk anywhere from where it opened
file_picker.j/k: move the cursor (arrows too, and ctrl+n / ctrl+p) — while nothing has been typed, and never in the save picker, where every letter is part of the name
file_picker.Enter: a folder: walk into it · a file: open it (a project) or land it on the pad (a sound)
file_picker.h: up one folder (left arrow too) — stops at the top of the filesystem and says so. In the save picker it is a letter; the left arrow and backspace-on-an-empty-name do the walking
file_picker.g/G: top / bottom of the list (open and sample pickers)
file_picker.typing: letters, digits, space, . - and _ narrow the list live (case-insensitive substring); backspace widens it again. From the first letter typed, j/k/h/g/G are letters and the arrows move the cursor — the footer changes to say so. Backspace on an empty filter goes up a folder
file_picker./: swap the list for the typed-path prompt this replaced — for paths no list can reach; esc closes that field. From the save picker it carries the name you had started typing into the field
file_picker.Esc: close, choosing nothing — in the save picker that cancels the save outright, and nothing is written
file_picker.takes: on a sampler, this session's own takes folder (<session>.samples/) is pinned at the top of the list when it exists, so a take recorded ten minutes ago is one Enter away
file_picker.memory: the folder you were last in is where the next picker opens, for as long as phosphor is running — so save-as after an open starts where you just were. The first picker of a run opens on the home folder
file_picker.empty: an empty projects folder says 'no projects yet · ctrl+s saves your first one here'; an empty samples folder says 'drop .wav files in this folder, or press / to type a path'; an empty folder in the save picker says 'nothing here yet · a name still saves into this folder' · a folder that cannot be read says so rather than looking empty

save_picker.description: space+s, and ctrl+s on a session that has never been saved. The open picker with a name line: the folders are walked the same way, the .phos files already there are listed dim for context, and what you type is the NAME rather than a filter. The file goes into the folder on the screen — the save and the list cannot disagree about where that is, which is the whole point of it.
save_picker.typing: every letter goes into the name, j k h g and G included — a name has to be able to start with any of them. The extension is shown dim after the cursor and added for you: type myjam, get myjam.phos
save_picker.arrows: ↑↓ (and ctrl+n / ctrl+p, PgUp / PgDn) move the cursor · ← goes up a folder, and so does backspace on an empty name
save_picker.Enter: with a name typed: saves it into the folder on the screen · with the name empty, on a folder: walks into it · with the name empty, on a project: takes THAT project's name into the name line, so one more Enter saves over it
save_picker.Backspace: takes back a character of the name · on an empty name, goes up a folder
save_picker.overwrite: saving onto a name already in the folder asks first — y writes it, n keeps the name and the list so you can edit it into a new one
save_picker.refusals: a path separator typed into the name is refused in words (press / to type a whole path) · Enter with no name and nothing under the cursor says 'type a name · or enter on a folder to go in' · a folder that will not take the write says so and the picker stays open, so you can walk somewhere that will
save_picker.Esc: cancels the save outright — nothing is written and the name is forgotten
save_picker./: the typed prompt behind the list, carrying whatever you had typed: a name goes into the folder the picker was showing, and a path with a separator in it is written exactly where it says

selected.y: yank (copy) clip (on a clip element); on the label: yank the track's whole arrangement
selected.p: paste clip after current (when on clip element; refuses to overlap)
selected.P: paste yanked clip(s) onto this track at the same bars (layering; refuses to overlap)
selected.D: duplicate the whole track — instrument, panel, effects, mix, clips — directly below (one undo step)
selected.n: on the label element: rename the track (trimmed, 8 chars max, undoable)

clip_locked.description: Enter on a clip enters this mode. h/l moves clip, Shift stretches, Ctrl trims.
clip_locked.h/l: move clip left/right by one beat
clip_locked.Shift+H/L: shrink/extend right edge by one beat
clip_locked.Ctrl+H/L: trim/extend left edge by one beat

volume_locked.description: Enter on the volume element enters this mode. The header cell shows the fader in dB relative to unity.
volume_locked.h/l: fader down/up by 1 dB (bottom = silent, unity = 0 dB, top = +6 dB)

tracks_pane.arm_display: an armed track's dot draws dim until the track is selected — MIDI records onto the selected track only

focus_switch.Tab: cycle tabs: trk fx → synth → inst config → piano → settings → trk fx

settings_tab.rec_quant: record quantize: off / 1/32 / 1/16 / 1/8 — takes snap to this grid as they commit; hits pulled onto one line collapse to the harder

clip_view.sequencer_child: the child knob on the pattern row picks what the sequencer drives — any instrument except another sequencer · pick the Sampler and it says 'the sampler needs its own track for pads': a kit lives on a track that IS a sampler, so a sequencer's child sampler has 88 empty pads, no [pads] tab and only its two globals; the [inst] panel says the same thing under its header

piano_roll_navigation.description: Default mode when viewing the piano roll (not in edit mode).
piano_roll_navigation.h/l: navigate columns (or MOVE highlighted notes left/right if highlights exist)
piano_roll_navigation.j/k: scroll up/down (or MOVE highlighted notes up/down if highlights exist)
piano_roll_navigation.Enter_with_highlights: lock highlights for STRETCHING (Right-Left-Trick on group)
piano_roll_navigation.Esc: clear highlights, or exit piano roll if no highlights
piano_roll_navigation.X: clear the clip's recorded controller data (mod wheel, pitch bend, aftertouch; undoable)
piano_roll_navigation.{ / }: jump the cursor down / up a whole octave (12 semitones) at once
piano_roll_navigation.[ / ]: snap the cursor to the nearest pitch below / above that has a note
piano_roll_navigation._framing: opening a clip frames the view on its notes, so you start on the music
piano_roll_navigation.g: jump the cursor to the playhead's column, landing on a sounding note there when one exists

piano_roll_highlight_locked.description: After highlighting notes and pressing Enter, h/l/H/L stretch the group.
piano_roll_highlight_locked.h/l: adjust LEFT edge of all highlighted notes
piano_roll_highlight_locked.H/L: adjust RIGHT edge of all highlighted notes

piano_roll_column_selected.description: Right-Left-Trick: column is locked. h/l adjusts note edges.
piano_roll_column_selected.h/l: adjust LEFT edge of all notes in column
piano_roll_column_selected.H/L: adjust RIGHT edge of all notes in column

piano_roll_row_mode.description: Single note selected via column→row drill-down.
piano_roll_row_mode.h/l: adjust LEFT edge of single note
piano_roll_row_mode.H/L: adjust RIGHT edge of single note

edit_mode.description: Space+E enters edit mode. Navigate between individual notes, select, move, delete.

navigate.j/k: move to next note UP/DOWN within same column
navigate.h/l: jump to nearest note in prev/next column
navigate.Enter: select cursor note for moving (single-note select)
velocity of the cursor note down/up by 8 (< / > by 24); the header shows the value

moving.trigger: plain direction after selecting, or Enter on a single note
moving.h/l: move selected notes left/right by grid step
moving.j/k: move selected notes up/down by semitone
moving.Shift+H/L: stretch RIGHT edge of selected notes (duration)
moving.Shift+J/K: stretch LEFT edge of selected notes (start position)
moving.Esc: lock notes in place, clear selection
velocity of the whole selection down/up (< / > in strides)

edit_mode.velocity_display: notes render brighter the harder they were hit, so dynamics are visible at a glance
edit_mode.m: toggle mute on the selection or cursor note — a muted note stays in the clip (drawn dark, struck through) but produces no sound; one undo step

quantize_modal.description: Space+Q opens quantize modal when a clip is selected.
quantize_modal.h/l: adjust selected value (grid resolution or strength %)

loop_editor.h/l: move loop start left/right by one grid step
loop_editor.H/L: move loop end left/right by one grid step
loop_editor.g: cycle the marker grid: bar / beat / 1/8 / 1/16
loop_editor.j/k: slide the whole brace forward/back by one grid step
loop_editor.J/K: leap the brace by its own length
loop_editor.x_or_d: cut the section (one undo across all tracks)
loop_editor.p: stamp at the brace (replaces under the stamp), then leapfrog

transport_pane.h/l: navigate transport elements (BPM, Record, Loop, Metronome)
transport_pane.Enter: activate element (edit BPM, toggle record, etc.)
transport_pane.count_in: Enter on the count element cycles off → 1 bar → 2 bars. With count-in set AND record armed (Space+r) AND play pressed — all three — the bars click down before recording rolls. R counts in too; any transport key during the countdown cancels it.
transport_pane.take_mode: Enter on the take element toggles overdub (passes layer up) vs re-record (R clears the loop range first, undoable); while recording the cell shows the running pass count
transport_pane.punch_in: R while the transport is already playing punches recording in at the playhead — no rewind, no count-in

grid_settings.snap: on/off — notes snap to grid when moved in edit mode

clip_behavior.shrink_right_edge: Notes past the new boundary are hidden (not deleted). Expanding restores them.
clip_behavior.trim_left_edge: Notes before the new start are hidden. Expanding restores them.
clip_behavior.move_clip: h/l in clip-locked mode. Collision detection prevents overlap.
clip_behavior.duplicate: d in clip-locked mode. Creates copy right after the clip.
clip_behavior.delete: Space+D with y/n confirmation. Selects adjacent clip after delete.
clip_behavior.piano_roll_sync: Clip view always shows the selected clip. Stretching/trimming updates piano roll in real time.

automation_lane.description: A in the piano roll opens a controller lane under the note grid, sharing the column grid so points sit under the notes in each column.
automation_lane.A: open the lane and give it the keys; A again hands them back to the note grid
automation_lane.k/j: raise/lower the controller value at the cursor column and draw a point (K/J = bigger steps)
automation_lane.h/l: walk columns; the value carries along, so a ramp is walk-right-and-raise
automation_lane.[ / ]: cycle which controller the lane shows (recorded streams first, then mod/bend/aftertouch)
automation_lane.d: clear the point in the cursor column
automation_lane.note: an empty clip offers mod, bend and aftertouch to draw from scratch; a recorded sweep opens on its own stream; edits are undoable and play back
automation_lane.r: ramp: draw both end values with k/j, then r fills every column back to the previous point with a straight line (one undo step)

midi_fx._about: MIDI effects run on the notes before the instrument, on live playing AND clip playback; recording stores the raw keys you played, never the generated notes — change the effect later and old takes play through the new setting
midi_fx.add: a in the [trk fx] tab (or enter on the fx cell) opens the add menu — 'arp · midi' is the MIDI entry; it lands above the audio effects in the same list
midi_fx.arp_panel: enter on the arp opens its panel: j/k picks a knob, h/l adjusts (H/L strides), b bypass, esc back
midi_fx.arp_params: style up/down/updown/played/chord/random · rate 1/4..1/32 incl. dotted+triplet · gate 1-200% · octaves 1-4 · latch off/hold (hold keeps the chord after hands leave; a new chord replaces it) · vel 0=as played or fixed · swing 50-75% (54/56/58 are the MPC feels)
midi_fx.bypass_remove: m (or b) mutes/bypasses the effect under the cursor — in the chain list and inside every panel (a muted MIDI effect flushes its held notes so nothing hangs); d removes with confirm, u undoes either
midi_fx.order: MIDI effects always lead the chain — they run on notes, the audio effects run on sound
midi_fx.chord_device: chord · midi: below the split every key plays its scale degree's full chord — root+scale pick the key, color picks triad/7th/9th/lush, voicing picks close/drop2/rootless A·B/quartal/spread, bass adds the root below, strum rolls it; a register lock voices each chord near the last so progressions walk
midi_fx.chain: chord before arp always (auto-ordered): one key → full chord → arpeggiated run
midi_fx.quality_movement: the minor→major→sus→dim magic: park the root, ride the color and scale knobs — every chord stays voiced near the last, so quality changes read as light changing, not jumps
midi_fx.ghost_notes: when a midi device is active, the piano roll draws its output as faint shaded notes behind your played notes — what you see is what will sound; they update as you turn knobs and vanish on bypass
midi_fx.commit: c in the [trk fx] tab prints the rack's output into the viewed clip as real editable notes and bypasses the devices (so it can't transform twice); one undo restores your played notes AND the live rack together
midi_fx.arp_presets: 1-4 in the arp panel: rhodes 8ths (up 1/8 gate75 swing56), dilla 16ths (played 1/16 gate45 swing58), wide updown (2 oct), chord pulse (1/8 gate40 swing54) — each one undo step
midi_fx.progression_mode: chord device mode knob: 'scale' (default, key = scale degree) or 'prog' — white keys walk a stored progression (C = first chord, D = second …, wrapping; black keys borrow the white below). prog knob picks from 8: 2-5-1 (Dm9 G13 Cmaj9), gospel V (G9sus4 G7b9 Cmaj9 C6/9), backdoor (Fm7 Bb9 Cmaj7), church IV→iv (Fmaj9 Fm6/9 Cmaj7/E), turnaround (A7b9 Dm9 G13sus4 Cmaj9), half-step (Dm9 Dbmaj7), neo loop (Bbm11 Gm9 Gbmaj13 Ebm11), quality cycle (Cm9 Cmaj9 C9sus4 C7b9 — one root, moving light). The root knob transposes every progression; the register lock keeps the voicings walking.
midi_fx.progression_editor: e in the chord panel opens the progression editor: j/k picks a chord row, tab picks the column (root/quality/bass), h/l turns it; a adds a chord (copies the cursor's), d removes, [ ] browses your saved library, n names it, s saves to the library (~/.phosphor/progressions.json), enter loads it into the device (flips mode to prog, prog to 'user'). 16 qualities to pick from — maj7/maj9/6-9/maj13, m7/m9/m11/m6-9, 7/9/13/9sus4, 7b9/7#9/mMaj7/dim7 — plus a slash bass per chord. Sessions store the resolved chords, so editing the library later never changes a saved song
midi_fx.humanize: the 'human' knob on both devices (0-100%): generated notes drag up to 10ms late and vary up to ±12 in velocity, like hands instead of a machine — steps never fire early, ghosts/commit stay deterministic
midi_fx.learn: r in the progression editor arms learn: play any chord on the controller and lift — the row becomes exactly that voicing, spread and all (root = lowest key). Turning its quality knob afterwards returns it to the dictionary. Learned chords save to the library and into sessions like any other
midi_fx.live_knobs: chord-shaping knobs (root, scale, color, voicing, bass, mode, prog — and loading a progression) re-voice chords that are ALREADY SOUNDING: removed tones release, new tones strike, common tones keep ringing. No need to stop/restart or re-press keys. Split, strum and human shape future presses only
midi_fx.split_warning: if a chord device is active and every note in the viewed clip is at/above the split, the status bar says so once — those notes pass through unchanged, which is why knobs would sound dead on them

sequencer_yank_paste.step: y with the cursor on the grid OR inside the step panel yanks the one step under it — pitch, chord, voicing, gate, accent; p drops it on the cursor position (one undo step). y on an empty step refuses
sequencer_yank_paste.pattern: y anywhere off the grid (the pattern/instrument row, the slots row) yanks the whole pattern as a block; p pastes it into the selected slot of whichever track's sequencer you're on — it crosses tracks and carries the notes, the length, the rate, everything (one undo step)

practice_room._about: spc+f on an instrument track opens 'fingers' — a jazz-piano technique trainer. Your MIDI controller keeps sounding the selected track's synth; the room listens with microsecond timestamps and judges. Everything is generated: no canned content, any key.
practice_room.drills: major scales, harmonic minor scales, chromatic (all with verified published fingerings, drawn on the keys), Hanon no.1, major arpeggios, shell ii-V-I around the cycle of fourths, rootless A/B ii-V-I, Charleston comping, bebop dominant scale, Barry Harris 6th-diminished chords, enclosures targeting 3rds
practice_room.keys: j/k drill · </> key in fourths · h hands (RH/LH/HT) · w wait/flow · c click (all beats / 2&4 jazz style / off) · [/] tempo · enter start/stop · esc leave
practice_room.modes: wait = time stops until you play the right note (chords need every voice down); flow = the metronome rolls and every onset is judged: perfect/good/early/late within a ±90ms window
practice_room.ladder: 3 clean reps in a row → tempo +5 BPM automatically; your best clean tempo is saved per drill+key+hand in ~/.phosphor/practice.json and you resume there next session
practice_room.metrics: bias (mean signed ms — rushing vs dragging), spread (consistency), evenness (IOI CV — under ~8% is conservatory-even), per-note verdict glyphs

loop_section._about: the loop brace is both a selection and a cursor: spc+l focuses it, and what's between the markers can be lifted and stamped anywhere
loop_section.grid: g cycles the marker grid: bar / beat / 1/8 / 1/16 — the brace can shrink to a single 1/16 (below that a loop is a buzz); display reads bars ('1-4') or positions ('1.2-1.3' = bar.beat, '1.1.2' adds the 16th)
loop_section.move: h/l move the start, H/L (or shift+h/l) the end, j/k slide the whole brace by one grid step, J/K leap it by its own length
loop_section.yank_cut: y lifts the section (all instrument tracks, notes+controllers whose ONSET is inside; tails travel whole); x (or d) lifts and removes — one undo step across every track
loop_section.paste: p stamps the lifted section at the brace start, REPLACING what's under the stamped span (and only the span — a track silent in the lift stamps its silence, tape-drop style), then leapfrogs the brace by the section length so p p p lays copies back to back; P layers instead of clearing (MPC-merge style). Clips union on landing, never overlap
loop_section.session: loop markers now save in ticks; old bar-based sessions load exactly as before

sampler._about: the sampler puts a sound on every piano key: 88 pads, each stacking up to eight wav layers, with its own trigger/poly/choke/cycle/pitch/ADSR and per-layer tune/trim/reverse/mute
sampler.create: space then a opens the instrument menu — pick Sampler; the track opens on its [pads] tab with the keys on it
sampler.pad_map: the keyboard band across the top IS the kit: a key with sounds on it lights in the track's colour and carries the number of layers, a key whose file went missing is red, and the caret ▼ marks the pad being edited · the bed scrolls to keep the caret in sight on a narrow terminal
sampler.pick_a_pad: play a key on your MIDI controller — the pad under that key becomes the current pad (C3 to start) · h/l walk the bed one key at a time, H/L by an octave
sampler.load: a opens the file picker on ~/.phosphor/samples/: j/k to a sound, enter lands it — type letters to narrow the list, h walks up a folder, and / swaps to the typed-path prompt (a bare name there looks in ~/.phosphor/samples/ and tries .wav for you). Each load stacks another layer on the current pad, up to eight, and points the panel at what just arrived
sampler.knobs: j/k picks a control, enter holds it, h/l turns it, H/L strides, esc lets go — held is the only time h/l stop walking the keyboard · the pad's own: trig · poly · choke · cycle · pitch · fine · attack · decay · sustain · release · level · pan · root · keytrk; then the selected layer's: level · pan · tune · fine · rev · mute
sampler.layers: [ and ] pick which sound on the pad the row knobs address, 1-8 jumps straight to one — one list, the wav/rec layers first and any phrases after them · m mutes the row (it keeps its seat) · d removes it and asks first · u brings it back with its audio or its notes, ctrl+r takes it off again
sampler.cycle: cycle turns the pad into a round robin: off (the default) every layer that answers the hit sounds and they stack, on exactly one of them answers and the next hit takes the next — eight snares on one key stop sounding like a machine gun · a muted layer and a layer outside the velocity window lose their turn rather than spending it on silence, so a velocity-split pad rotates each half on its own · phrases are never cycled: every phr row on the pad fires either way, because a phrase is note traffic for the shared child and not one of several takes of a sound · where the rotation has got to is the pad's memory: stopping the transport does not put it back to layer one, and neither does editing the pad — only the panic key does · it is a zone's control too, and it goes into the session
sampler.audition: moving the layer cursor with [ ] or 1-8 plays that sound on its own, outside the pad's poly and choke — a muted layer stays silent, and the audition stops the moment you leave the pads tab
sampler.trim: t on a layer that has audio opens the trim strip: the whole file as a waveform, the region that plays lit and the cut ends dark, [ and ] over the two markers · h/l move the START, H/L move the END — the loop brace's grammar · every start nudge plays the region from its new start
sampler.trim_unit: j/k walk how far one press moves: bar · beat · 1/16 · 10ms · 1ms · 1 sample (j deeper, k wider; it opens on 10ms) — the musical units come from the transport tempo measured against the layer's OWN sample rate, so a bar of a 48k loop is a bar wherever it is played
sampler.trim_switches: z toggles the zero-crossing snap (on by default: an edge lands on the nearest sign change within 5ms, and keeps the frame you asked for when there is none) · w pulls BOTH markers onto the audible part of the recording — the same −48 dB in / 8 ms back / −60 dB out / 20 ms after that a fresh take is trimmed by, so a take that opens on a second of room tone (or a reversed one that ends on it) is one press away from hugging its sound; one press of u puts both markers back, a second w says the edges are already there, and a recording with nothing in it refuses in words · r plays the region backwards · t loops it while you work · esc goes back to the pad map and stops the sound — esc is the only way out, and Tab is swallowed the way it is under a held knob, because the strip owns every key while it is open
sampler.trim_limits: the edges never cross and stop a millisecond apart, which it says in words · a whole nudge run is one press of u · a layer whose file is missing is refused rather than trimmed
sampler.trim_picture: under the pad panel, when the pane has the rows for it: the same waveform three rows tall — the whole buffer, the region that plays lit and the cut ends dark, the [ and ] markers under them, and 'rev' in the margin when the layer plays backwards · it is a look and nothing else: no key addresses it, t is still the editor, and a phrase row or a layer whose file has gone shows its own words instead · it is the first thing a short pane drops, because the keyboard band and the controls outrank a picture of them
sampler.hear_it: press the same key — the pad plays its layers together; one-shot pads play whole, retriggers cut the last hit with a fade
sampler.resample: i on a pad asks which of our own instruments to record it from (everything except the sequencer and the sampler itself) — the track starts playing that instrument, the banner says so, and the pad cursor freezes because your keys are a performance now · p swaps what r will land, audio or phrase, and the banner reads it out · esc puts the sampler back with its kit · while the mode is on the sampler is out of the track's plugin slot, so every key that edits a PAD is refused in words rather than acted on — space included, from any tab
sampler.resample_panel: Tab off the pad map and the [inst] panel is the SOURCE instrument's for as long as the mode is on — its patch selector, its knobs, its names, headed 'DX7 · source for pad C3' so you can see whose panel you are in · j/k pick a control and h/l turn it, the same keys as any other track's panel, and you hear every turn immediately because that instrument IS the track's plugin slot · the patch knob loads a whole patch here exactly as it does anywhere else · the sampler's own level/vel are not on this panel while the mode is on, and cannot be moved from it · esc on the panel backs out to the track list, not out of the mode (the mode's esc is on the pads tab, where the banner offering it is) · what you dial is what r renders the take through, and the pad keeps it: landing a take, leaving the mode, or pressing i again writes the panel onto the pad in one undo step named 'pad source panel' — and only if you actually moved something · Space+W's preset browser is not reachable while the mode is on, because space is refused; the factory patch selector is how you pick a sound here
sampler.resample_take: r arms, r again ends the take and lands it on the pad as a rec layer, selected and named 'take 1', 'take 2' — stopping the transport ends it too, and esc ends a running take before it leaves the mode · the flash gives the length and the peak · one press of u takes it back off, ctrl+r brings it back with its audio
sampler.resample_timing: with the transport stopped the take is free: it starts on your first note, ends when you disarm, and the instrument's tail is rendered out to silence (2s at most, auto-trimmed −48 dB in / −60 dB out) · rolling, it is bar-quantised: the window opens at the next bar line and closes at the end of the bar you disarm in, so the take is whole bars and LOOPS — nothing past the loop point is kept, and nothing is trimmed
sampler.resample_how: what is recorded is MIDI with its arrival stamps; the audio is rendered afterwards, offline, through a fresh copy of the instrument and the track's own chord/arp devices — deterministic, so the same performance renders the same samples every time · caps: 60s free, 64 bars rolling, and a full pad refuses the arm before you play
sampler.resample_root: a performance on one key teaches the pad its root (keytrk is left alone — a root is a fact, keytracking is a decision); a chord leaves the root where it was · the pad keeps what it was recorded from, and says so: the panel carries a '◎ source: DX7 · i records more' line, the filled-pad list marks the pad with ◎ and names the mark in its head wherever the column fits, and leaving the mode ends with 'i returns to DX7' · i reopens the picker titled 'source for C3 · now: dx7', standing on that instrument with '· this pad's source' beside it, and the panel you recorded with still on it
sampler.normalize: n on a rec or wav layer sets its level so the trimmed region peaks at −0.5 dB — a gain value, never a rewrite of the audio · n again puts the level back to unity · our instruments render with a lot of headroom, so a quiet take can run out of level control (+12 dB) and the flash says how far short it landed
sampler.phrases: a phrase is the performance kept as notes instead of audio, replayed live through one instrument — four bars cost a few hundred events rather than a few megabytes · in source mode press p until the banner reads 'take: phrase', then r, play, r: the notes land on the pad as a phr row, chord/arp devices baked in exactly as they are for audio, one press of u deep · a one-finger phrase teaches the pad its root, and the pad remembers audio-or-phrase with the instrument it was recorded from
sampler.phrases_child: ONE child instrument per sampler, not one per pad — every phrase on every pad plays through it, so it is rendered once a block however many are running · landing a phrase points it at the instrument that phrase was played on, panel and all, and if that is a different instrument from the one it was pointed at the flash says 'child is now X · every phrase plays through it' · the child goes into the session and comes back with it
sampler.phrases_controls: a phrase's own controls are vel (the velocity scale every note is multiplied by, 0-400%, shown as a percentage because it scales what is played and not how loud the result is), mute, and keytrk (transpose by the played key's distance from the pad's root) · the pad's level, pan and ADSR do NOT reach a phrase and are not drawn as if they do, and neither do pan, tune or rev — there is one shared render for every phrase on the kit, so there is nowhere per-phrase to put them · choke, poly, one-shot/gate and the panic key all reach a phrase the way they reach a sample
sampler.phrases_list: phr rows sit after the wav/rec rows in the same list: name, length in seconds (frames at the engine's rate — the tempo you played at is baked in, a phrase does not follow a tempo change), the vel percentage, phr, and a mute dot · moving the cursor onto one does not audition it — a phrase has no waveform to sound on its own, so it says to press the pad's key instead · t on a phr row says a phrase is notes rather than opening an empty waveform · a phr row marked 'no instrument' is a sampler with no child, which only a hand-edited session can produce
sampler.keys_mode: K switches the bed between pads (every key its own sound) and keys (stretches of keys playing one sound, transposed from a root) — capital and deliberate, because lowercase k walks the knob cursor · both truths are kept: the pad map is still there under the zones and comes back untouched when you press K again, and the session file stores both
sampler.keys_zones: w covers the whole bed with one zone · o covers the octave the caret is in · s splits the zone under the caret at the caret key (the left half keeps its root, the right is rooted at its own first key) · inside a zone, w and o move that zone's edges instead of laying a second one over it · a new zone is seeded with the sound on the pad under the caret, or empty if there is none — then a loads one into it
sampler.keys_brace: the span is the first control on the panel: enter holds it, then h/l move the LOW edge and H/L the HIGH one — the loop brace's grammar, so H/L are the other end and not a stride · an edge stops where its neighbour begins and never pushes it, and stops at the ends of the bed · a whole run of presses is one press of u
sampler.keys_zone_list: the column beside the panel becomes the zone list: span, sound, layer count, root and how many keys · the band grows a rule under the keyboard drawing each zone's brace, with ┼ where its root is and ◆ on the root key itself
sampler.keys_drop: D takes the zone under the caret off the bed after a y/n confirmation — capital, because lowercase d still removes a layer from the zone's sound · u brings the zone back with its audio
sampler.keys_root: a root arrives three ways: a one-pitch take teaches it, a file name that ends in a note teaches it on the way in (Piano_C3, kick_A#1, Strings Eb2 — a name that is not a note changes nothing, and C3loop is not a note), or R arms the keyboard and the next key played becomes the root · esc disarms · the bar blinks ROOT? while it is armed, and the key played does not move the caret
sampler.keys_edits: everything else is the same keys pointed at the zone instead of the pad: j/k walks its controls, [ ] picks a sound inside it, t trims, n normalizes, i records into it · keytrk is not offered, because a zone always tracks the keyboard · where two zones overlap their layers stack, the ninth is turned away and the flash says so
sampler.sessions: saving stores each layer's path (never the audio); a file that moved is kept on its pad, marked red on the bed and 'missing' in the layer list — fix the path or drop the file in samples/ and reopen
sampler.sessions_takes: a recorded take has no file until you save: the save writes it as a 32-bit float WAV into <session>.samples/ beside the session file and stores the path relatively, so the project folder can be moved or copied whole · takes already on disk are not rewritten, saving under a new name gives the new project its own copies, and a take whose wav has gone missing keeps its pad and turns red like any other · the same save sweeps out the takes the kit no longer names — only inside that folder and only files it wrote itself, so a wav you put there by hand is left alone
sampler.memory: the head of the pad list (and of the zone list) says how much audio the kit is holding — '12.3 MB held' — counting a buffer shared by several pads once, so a zone across the whole bed costs one sample and not eighty-eight · it is not there at all on an empty kit
sampler.presets: space then w saves and loads the sampler's two globals, level and vel, and nothing else: the pads, layers, zones and takes are the session's, not a preset bank's, and loading a preset leaves the kit exactly where it was
